bib.title: From LLM to Conversational Agent: A Memory Enhanced Architecture with Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

question: How can an LLM be turned into a controllable multi-turn conversational agent by extending ReAct with a scratchpad and retrieved examples as working memory, and by fine-tuning on a small curated dataset?
hypothesis: Adding a Scratchpad (short-term memory) and retrieved Examples (long-term memory) to ReAct, and fine-tuning instead of prompting, improves quality, controllability and efficiency.
contributions: RAISE, an enhancement of ReAct that uses scratchpad and retrieved examples to augment the agent's capabilities.
A fine-tuning scenario for LLMs within RAISE that, compared with prompts alone, enhances controllability, effectiveness and efficiency.
Experiments on an in-house real-estate sales dataset showing RAISE's superiority as a conversational agent.

method.summary: RAISE keeps a working memory of system prompt, conversation history, task trajectory, scratchpad (dialogue-level key-value store of tool observations and entities) and top-k retrieved examples (turn-level, vector retrieval from an example pool of <Q,A> pairs) in a ReAct loop with 12 tools. Training data are built from real conversations by selection, scene extraction, GPT-4 CoT completion with manual validation, and scene augmentation, then Qwen-14B-Chat is fully fine-tuned. Five frameworks (Act-Only, ReAct, +Scratchpad, +Examples, RAISE) are compared under prompting (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Qwen) and fine-tuning (Qwen).
method.task: multi-turn conversational agent with tool use (real estate sales IM)

datasets.name: In-house Beike real-estate IM scenes
datasets.source: Authentic anonymised dialogues from Beike; in-house, not stated as public
datasets.preprocessing: Conversation selection (scene completion, minimum turns, quality, user-message ratio), anonymisation, one scene per turn, sampling by turn count and intent, GPT-4 CoT generation plus manual validation, augmentation with Information Missing and Capability Mismatch scenes. Scratchpad and Examples content varied 20% empty, 30% partial, 50% full.

other.use: prompting; also generates all fine-tuning CoT data; ChatCompletion mode, as of November 2023, temperature 0.5

training.objective: Supervised fine-tuning on Sample = SystemPrompt + History + Query + CoT (Thought, Action, Observation) + Response; full-parameter

other.training_hardware_note: only inference hardware (1x A100 80GB) is stated
other.one_shot: prompting uses a one-shot example for structured output; fine-tuning omits it

inference.samples: inferred: one run per scene; not stated
inference.prompting: System prompt with profile, task instruction, 12 tool descriptions, one-shot example, then history and query (Tables 5-9). Steps per framework: Act-Only (Action, Observation, Finish); ReAct (Thought, Action, Observation, Finish); +Scratchpad; +Examples; RAISE (Scratchpad, Examples, Thought, Action, Observation, Finish).
inference.retrieval: top-k relevant examples recalled from the Example Pool by vector retrieval over history and current query; k and embedding model not stated

parameters.stop_criteria: enough information, preset loop limit exceeded, or system error (limit value not stated)

metrics.name: Specificity
metrics.definition: 0-2 human score: vague (0), some specifics (1), detailed and direct (2)

metrics.name: Naturalness
metrics.definition: 0-2: mechanical (0), somewhat stiff (1), smooth and human-like (2)

metrics.name: Ov. Qual. Score
metrics.definition: inferred: sum of the four quality scores (max 8)

metrics.name: Inference Speed
metrics.definition: Average time to process each user query

baselines: prompting GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Qwen-14B-Chat vs fine-tuned Qwen-14B-Chat
eval.protocol: Quality scored by human annotation; efficiency by statistics. GPT API speed omitted. Annotator count, agreement, blinding, seeds and significance tests are not stated.

limits: Evaluation is on one in-house real-estate dataset of 100 held-out scenes; dataset, code and weights are not released.
Quality scores are human annotations with no stated annotator count, agreement, blinding or significance test; single run, no seeds.
Fine-tuning data were generated by GPT-4 and the GPT-4 prompting baseline shares that origin; training hardware, optimiser, retrieval k and embedding model are not stated.
The memory components are ablated only as a bundle per framework; memory is not tested over long conversations or against other memory designs.
The authors concede 'potential hallucination issues and challenges in handling complex logic problems'.
Speed claims for fine-tuned vs prompted are asserted in prose; GPT API speed was omitted and prompting-Qwen speed is not tabulated.
Quality differences between frameworks are small (7.5 to 7.72 under GPT-4), so the ranking may be within noise.

terms.definition: Logs background information, knowledge generated by reasoning and observations from previous tool usage; dialogue-level; likened to short-term memory
Query-response pairs recalled from the Example Pool to supplement knowledge gaps and customise behaviour; turn-level; the retrieval module acts as long-term memory
System prompt, conversation history, task trajectory, scratchpad and examples together
The tuned agent retains broad LLM skills (e.g. Python coding) that conflict with its role; countered with Capability Mismatch scenes
Incorrect statements from inadequate or misapplied pretraining knowledge; countered with Information Missing scenes
